chunks: Zurarah and al-Fuḍayl said: We said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Have you considered the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"Indeed, salat (prayer) has been decreed upon the believers as a prescribed ordinance at appointed times."

He said: "It means a prescribed obligation, and it does not mean the time of its lapse. If that time passed and then he performed it, it would not be a prayer performed on time. If that were so, then Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd عليه السلام would have perished when he performed it outside its time. Rather, whenever he remembered it, he performed it."

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), the obligatory ritual prayer under discussion

ai.seo_question: Does Qur'an 4:103 mean that a missed prayer is no longer valid after its appointed time?
ai.summary: Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام explains that the verse means salat (prayer) is a prescribed obligation upon the believers. He clarifies that the verse does not mean a missed prayer becomes invalid in an absolute sense, but that if performed after its time it is no longer counted as performed on time. The narration also cites Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd عليه السلام as evidence that a prayer remembered later is still to be performed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.606 – Zurarah and Al-Fudail said:
"We asked Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir (as)) about the statement of Allah (swt), the Mighty Majestic:
'Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a timed decree' (Surah An-Nisa 4:103).

Imam (as) replied: "It means that it is an obligatory decree (prescribed prayer) and does not refer to a specific cut-off time after which it would not be valid. If one misses the prescribed time and then performs the prayer, it would not be considered a timely (adā') prayer. If this were so, then Sulayman ibn Dawud (Solomon (as)) would have been destroyed when he prayed outside its prescribed time, but rather, whenever he remembered it, he performed it."
